What the Fog

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Half a billion rand was spent cleaning schools potentially infected with covid, the method used - fogging - is scientifically unproven, turns out this was just dirty corruption.

Unique Selling Point:
2,300-3000 Gauteng schools were supposedly cleaned when schools went back last year after lockdown level 4 opened. (Thousands of school children and teachers, cleaners etc and unions were concerned about covid – everyone was panicking and so the Gauteng dept of education decided to clean schools – a decision was made to fog them, once they were fogged a "certificate of cleaning" was given to the school by the service provider). Despite the National dept of health issuing an advisory (second page) against fogging – as it doesn’t work, and they don’t require a certificate of cleaning (The certificate of cleaning came about when service providers were issuing these meaningless certificates that you have no covid… “guarantee that there’s no covid in the place we just cleaned... which is an insane thing to promise)

Health experts, papers, reports around the world say fogging doesn’t work – no scientific evidence, and that normal cleaning and disinfection is best. Its never been recommended either by our local cleaning industry. We will show these normal cleaning methods...

Contract never went out, they used the emergency procurement issue to sidestep the process. And 6 companies awarded these cleaning tenders worth R431 million just for the schools, and later on some provincial buildings R117 million which took the figure to over half a billion.

95% profit margin in this work according to bath… 40 million – only 2 million doing work…they’ve done costing…

THE COMPANIES:
The SIU are dealing with three batches – Asset forfeiture for over R40 million – KZN doctors – who were awarded contracts in gauteng… get names listed… main indiv. Dr Bright Mhalangu – director of 30 companies – the entity awarded the majority of the work had R1000 in its bank account and it received 11 million from gde. They find out that it was aid for jewellery, cars, watches, investment policies, paying off bonds. Source: Typically this is for labour, equipment and consumables.
Second batch – R20 million
3rd batch – whistle-blower one of them… consulted in general. Work in progress. Only 5% would be actual costs… worse than the PPE one, they had to buy the masks…
The Gauteng Exp disclosure report (publicised in daily maverick) was the key document – came out in sometime in early jan. This showed who got the contracts. Mark Heywood…
A lot of these companies were est relatively recently, and have no track record. They weren’t included with NCCA – PAYING BELOW minimum wage, didn’t make contributions to industry for em – weren’t in accordance to regulations in the land.
They select someone from CID (national treasury database) paul roux screen shots of suppliers…– they weren’t even on there, and if they were on there it was just before. Clearly handpicked… (paul roux – with documents)
Logical conclusion is that they were politically connected…



Summary:
KEO Group – paid R39.9-million
KEO Group’s website bills the company as “an electrical mechanical and civil engineering also in the business of cleaning and hygiene services as well as smart technology sensitizer dispenser supplies and installation. We also offer services in project management, technical advisory and tender document management.”
The website details offering “microbial fogs”. Among the claims are that these “prevent the build-up of pathogens … All have been tested and documented by the South African Bureau of Standards.” [There is no list or reference for this claim.]
In correspondence project manager Geoffrey Nyathi said the company charged R10.25 per metre and did work for GDID over 27 weeks. The company’s current sole director is registered as 25-year-old Phetogo Molefe. Her name, however, doesn’t appear on the employee list Nyathi provided. The business address is listed as 87 Booysens Road, Booysens, in Johannesburg, and also indicates its address as unit numbers in an “Xspace” storage facility on the same street.
If you visist both sites; one appeared to be a tyre workshop and the other a storage unit warehouse. The KEO Group website gallery shows uncaptioned photographs of what it states are examples of its projects. There is only one captioned picture on the website, of a person in a hazmat suit appearing to fog an office. It states “Kempton Park Department of Social Development” and is dated 23 June 2020.


Further information:
Industry sources say the KEO Group does not have a track record in the office cleaning industry, that it has a very small number of employees and does not contract out its work, raising questions about it’s ability to have carried out the work for which it received the tender. The sources also allege that KEO has several outstanding compliance issues, including paying legislated pay rates, statutory contributions to the SARS skills levy and provident fund contributions.
Cocase South Africa – paid R33.7-million Cocase South Africa is registered to Carol Cebile Blake and the business address is a house on Ivan Street in Kempton Park. The company’s online profile is a Facebook page. Its most recent post was a recruitment advertisement on 27 May 2020 for two environmental project managers. The page includes a link to a company website but this link is broken.
Ambroser Solutions – paid R28.8-million The sole director of the company is listed as 32-year-old Simtholile Ambitious Ndlovu. The company was registered in February 2015 to an address in Highveld Park, Emalahleni, Mpumalanga. Ambroser Solutions’s only web presence turns out to be a listing with the National Contract Cleaning Association. It appears under “cleaner” with a physical address stated as Waterfront Blue Gill, 12 Dabchick Close, Kempton Park. The address doesn’t show up on a location map.
Lucage Trading and Projects – paid R10.5-million This company has two directors listed as Magdeline Kagiso Kwele, 33, and Nsizwa Louis Mahlangu, 37, of Hatfield, Pretoria, and Pretoria West respectively. Their business address for Lucage Trading and Projects is listed as Chromeville Street in Mhluzi, Mpumalanga and the business was registered in June 2016. The email for the pair is registered to a university student number email. There is no web presence for the company though Lucage Trading and Projects appears on a public business listing site. There is no physical or postal address or contact details given here either.
TES Cleaning – paid R3.8-million TES Cleaning was registered in November 2019. Its sole director is named as 38-year-old Kathy Singh of Douglasdale, Johannesburg. There is no web presence for the company and no publicly available contact details.
The over R190-million spent by the GDID does not include the R431-million spent by the Gauteng Education Department on sanitising schools, which is still being investigated by the Special Investigating Unit (SIU).
There were many more…

RENTOKILL – fogging and another company that does fogging - we will ask them to show us fogging... need visuals...
CDC video clip states it unequivocally … it does not work


Mark Heywood: Then we received 1 or 2 extra reports, and then we came across the fact that the figures were inaccurate, out by R250,000. (mark’s article) – this was directed back to Gauteng treasury. Needed to go back to their figures. Then the disclosure reports went silent. Via PAIA by Kirsten at CW they will release it end of June.

Bidvest prestige clean and disinfect 1,000 schools free of charge.

Kirsten from corruption watch:
Never seen such a quick reaction to paia request… lit a fire under the asses…
We suspect they’ve still paid suppliers for de-fogging. But there has likely been a curtailing effect…def for jan/feb…
Had they not been as active – in 2nd and 3rd waves to defog buildings and schools… central Johannesburg provisional buildings… paul roux…

Pay researcher Mark Heywood for his initial research like the erin/jan stories

Mark Heywood Researcher/Journalist
Arthur Bath Cleaning Industry rep & Whistleblower
Paul Roux Whistleblower

Press Release:


What the Fog?

Scientists say that sterilising surfaces with disinfecting liquids and wipes is enough to reduce exposure to the virus that causes COVID-19, so why did an already cash-strapped Gauteng Department of Education spend nearly half a billion Rands on a controversial fogging method as schools were set to open after lockdown last year? As the Special Investigating Unit refers 63 state employees to various institutions for disciplinary action for contravening supply chain regulations and the Public Finance Management Act, Carte Blanche investigates the haphazard awarding of emergency tenders on cleaning contracts that delivered little of value in empty classrooms.

Producer: Sasha Schwendenwein | Presenter: Derek Watts

Script:


Personal protective equipment is necessary to fight Covid-19. But when it comes to cleaning a virus that cannot be seen, some saw an opportunity to also clean the government of nearly half a billion rands.
THE LOST BILLIONS IN DODGY PPE DEALS HAVE LEFT US SICK TO THE STOMACH...BUT THERE WAS IN MOST CASES SOMETHING TO SHOW FOR IT...VASTLY OVERPRICED MASKS AND SANITISERS. BUT THEN IT SEEMS CAME THE PERFECT PLOY...
The Gauteng Department of Education’s plan to sanitize 237 classrooms by deep cleaning, decontamination and fogging sounded reasonable, as teachers, parents and unions cried out against going back to school in July last year. But it was in that panic, that emergency tender procurement measures allowed R431 million rands’ worth of cleaning contracts to be allocated to 280 companies.
Upsound mark Heywood:” going through all the amounts going to contractors…”
Human rights and social justice activist Mark Heywood has reported on health and basic education for over 20 years. As the editor of “maverick citizen”, while investigating the PPE scandal, he came across the Gauteng legislature’s Covid-19 Expenditure Disclosure reports from October to December 2020.
The first month they reported,90 million rand. And I thought, that's crazy. //They reported another, I think, two hundred million rand. And I thought that's even crazier. What is going on?
The world health organization doesn’t recommend fogging for covid-19 because it’s ineffective in removing the virus outside of the direct spray zone.
WHAT IS STAGGERING ABOUT THESE TENDERS AND THE AMOUNTS PAID FOR THE APPARENTLY USELESS FOGGING IS THAT THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH PUT OUT AN ADVISORY IN JUNE LAST YEAR SAYING IT DOES NOT ENDORSE DEEP CLEANING, WHICH INCLUDES FOGGING.
Nobody was saying anything about this, why is there no outcry?
But Arthur Bath and his professional cleaning industry colleagues were crying fowl!
A: There's not a single member of the formal associations in the cleaning industry that received one of these contracts,
D: If Foggy doesn't work, what methods should have been used to clean the schools?
You just wipe down the surfaces with disinfectant detergent, covid-19 is one of the easiest microorganisms and viruses to inactivate through normal cleaning.
SO THIS IS A ROOM BEFORE FOGGING....AND THIS IS THE SAME ROOM AFTER FOGGING. SPOT THE DIFFERENCE. WELL YOU ARE RIGHT...THERE IS NO DIFFERENCE.
Bath, a 40 year cleaning industry veteran, reported this to the State Investigating unit or SIU, as did Gauteng Education MEC Panyaza Lesufi. They’d all read Heywoods reports. Within months, SIU spokesperson Kaizer Kganyago confirmed the tender processes were irregular.
There were people who just sent WhatsApp messages to be appointed and they were appointed. We found that there was no value for money; it was said by the Department of Health that the covid sits on substances for at least a week and the schools have not been with people for over five months at that time.
The contracts were also NOT structured on square meterage, but instead a thumb sucked figure of between R250,000 to R300,000 PER SCHOOL.
Derek: What would the estimated profit margin have been on these cleaning and fogging jobs?
Somewhere between 5 and 10% of the 431 million would have been the actual cost. All the rest was profit.
D: Is there any evidence that they were done?
According to the department, they did get signatures from the personnel at the schools after the fogging was done.
Schools were issued with “A Certificate of Cleaning” – a seemingly frivolous piece of paper that the Department of Health doesn’t endorse as no entity can guarantee a place is covid free. Patrick Nndwamato began as a cleaner himself working his way up to become CEO of his own company – Cleaning Africa.
How did you feel when you found out that millions were being awarded to and clean schools and you weren't getting any part of it?
It was a hard pill to swallow because as a business that complies with every legislation we obviously did not get to that opportunity.
D: What would be an average quote?
I would say roughly R2-R4.50 per square meter.
So my math is right, just over R10,000,
P: Just over 10000, and there is no way you can do it for R200,00. It’s a scam.
The SIU found that few contractors were registered with the Central Supplier Database or CSD - an approved list of government service providers.
One of the things we found is out of 280 companies think about 173 were not on the CSD And for us it's a problem because then you find car washes, find companies that you don't understand how they go to this? We found that the money got in and they are spending it like hotcakes. And for us, it was a concern if we wait for the end of the investigation, this money wouldn't be there. Therefore, it's better we then go and block this amount of money before it gets out of the accounts
In early June the SIU approached the Special Tribunal which was set up by the National Prosecuting Authority to fast-track high profile cases. Carte Blanche accessed the preservation orders issued to freeze bank accounts and assets to the value of R40.7 million of 14 service providers, this was followed a week later by 7 more companies with assets worth R22.4 million.
The SIU investigators highlighted several characters in their affidavits, like Durban HIV researcher Dr Sigwile Bright Mhlongo, whose four companies [Insimu Projects, which was awarded a R13.9m contract; Insimu Consulting (R11.5m); Mangaliso Projects (R11.6m); and Insimu Medical Group (R4.6m)] received R41 million. His businesses are part of a Durban-based Foundation which owns several hospitals and businesses [Umlazi Private Hospital, Roodepoort Urogynae Hospital, a paramedic company, an agricultural foundation, medical equipment and linen manufacturing companies and Men's Sexual Health Clinics SA.] It’s co-directors are Fikile Eugenia Mpofana and Dr Njabulo Mabaso who share a property in this Dainfern estate. Two of Mpofana's companies scored contracts worth R15.5m [Fikile Mpofana 11.6m and Lisondalo 3.9m] and were registered shortly before the awarding of the tenders. Lindokuhle Mkhize whose company, Mhlongo was a former director of, landed a R6.7m contract. After which Mkhize transferred R2.3m to Mhlongo. In a matter of weeks, 30 year old Mpofana and Dr Mhlongo burnt through over R40. In late October, Mpofana paid off her house (R705,000) bought a designer watches (R399,000 on Baume & Mercier watches at RLG Africa jewellers), jewellery (R190,800 on jewellery at Arthur Kaplan), a Mercedez Benz (R1.7m payment to EB Motors Klerksdorp for a Mercedes-Benz V-Class van) and plastic surgery (R143,000 to Johannesburg plastic surgeon Dr Deon Weyers). One of Mhlongo’s company bank accounts had just R1,000 in it before the department paid R11.6m. His spending included millions in investment policies, R2.5m payment into a Liberty Group policy; R3.5m payment into an Investec Wealth and Investment account), and two vehicles (R1.4m to EB Motors Klerksdorp for a Mercedes-Benz V-Class van, R775,037 for a Range Rover Sport)
We called Dr Mhlongo and Fikile Mpofana.
Mhlongo: “I can’t comment now as its under investigation.
S: But you understand why people are upset, because it’s public money?
Please speak to my lawyer.”
S: “Do you have anything you want to add?
Mpofana: No nothing. Thank-you.”
Lawyer Siphile Buthelezi represents all of those we’ve named. They declined to comment and will file their responses to these allegations in court in due course.
Buthelezi“The SIU has not plead any wrongdoing from our clients,
S: Did your clients have any relationship with the department?
B: They didn’t know anyone there. There’s 280 companies that were awarded.”
In writing he added: "....the allegations are denied.”
THE BIG QUESTION IS WHO SHOULD BE HELD ACCOUNTABLE? SOMEONE MADE THE DECISIONS WITHIN THE GAUTENG DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION 1. AS TO WHICH SERVICE PROVIDERS WOULD BE AWARDED THESE CONTRACTS, AND 2. THAT THE CLEANING METHOD WOULD PREDOMINANTLY BE FOGGING.
Digging into the SIUs affidavits a Gauteng education department employee claims Nkhensani Hudson Baloyi was the one issuing instructions.
AS HEAD OF DEPARTMENT EDWARD MOSUWE SIGNED OFF ON THE PROCUREMENT PROCESSES AND REVIEWED THE PAYMENTS. WHAT HAS HE GOT TO SAY?
Mosuwe: “I’m in a meeting… I’m waiting for investigation and report.”
Mosuwe’s mandate is to report everything to MEC Lesufi.
Whilst, there is a separation of powers between the political head, and the administrative head, the head of department, that there has to be oversight.
Carte Blanche approached Corruption Watch researcher Kirsten Pearson to request any meeting minutes that can indicate when the decisions were made and by whom.
D: Has it been a reversal in transparency in regards to procurement information?
Yes, unfortunately, the expenditure disclosure reports for helping have not been put out since January. It's now June. They were incredibly quick to respond they will be published after being audited. We hope they've not been editing the reports after all this time.
The Gauteng Education Department responded on behalf of Baloyi and management saying it prefers to wait for the SIUs report before commenting… ”We eagerly await the findings and recommendations of the report so that we can act on them.”
The Public Finance Management Act gives us some clues as to who should be held accountable. The accounting officer is the head of department and those who were involved in writing up the terms of reference for the work.
Heywood made an additional discovery in the Gauteng expenditure disclosure report figures.
M: I was able to pick up in the last of the reports that I analyzed a miscalculation of two hundred and fifty million rand, they were faithfully reproduced by the national treasury as if they were accurate, what's to stop the person, a person or persons dipping in at a later point and saying, well, they inflated by two hundred and fifty million rand, it's been accepted. We can now go and cash in on some of this money.
The SIU wants to develop new laws in order to pursue corrupt officials' assets. Their investigations will be handed to the NPA who can then prosecute.
We don't investigate people. we're investigating the contract between the department and those service providers. And if in the process we find the people we're calling them and hear their side of the story from the lowest level to the highest level. if the evidence leads us to you, we will come to you.
On Wednesday this week, a third batch of asset seizures involving 5 new companies worth R4.5million was successfully granted. Bringing the total to over R67 million that the SIU are attempting to recoup.

Nobody was saying anything about this, why is there no outcry? But Arthur Bath and his professional cleaning industry colleagues were crying fowl! A: There's not a single member of the formal associations in the cleaning industry that received one of these contracts, D: If Foggy doesn't work, what methods should have been used to clean the schools? You just wipe down the surfaces with disinfectant detergent, covid-19 is one of the easiest microorganisms and viruses to inactivate through normal cleaning. SO THIS IS A ROOM BEFORE FOGGING....AND THIS IS THE SAME ROOM AFTER FOGGING. SPOT THE DIFFERENCE. WELL YOU ARE RIGHT...THERE IS NO DIFFERENCE. Bath, a 40 year cleaning industry veteran, reported this to the State Investigating unit or SIU, as did Gauteng Education MEC Panyaza Lesufi. They’d all read Heywoods reports. Within months, SIU spokesperson Kaizer Kganyago confirmed the tender processes were irregular. There were people who just sent WhatsApp messages to be appointed and they were appointed. We found that there was no value for money; it was said by the Department of Health that the covid sits on substances for at least a week and the schools have not been with people for over five months at that time. The contracts were also NOT structured on square meterage, but instead a thumb sucked figure of between R250,000 to R300,000 PER SCHOOL. Derek: What would the estimated profit margin have been on these cleaning and fogging jobs? Somewhere between 5 and 10% of the 431 million would have been the actual cost. All the rest was profit. D: Is there any evidence that they were done? According to the department, they did get signatures from the personnel at the schools after the fogging was done. Schools were issued with “A Certificate of Cleaning” – a seemingly frivolous piece of paper that the Department of Health doesn’t endorse as no entity can guarantee a place is covid free. Patrick Nndwamato began as a cleaner himself working his way up to become CEO of his own company – Cleaning Africa. How did you feel when you found out that millions were being awarded to and clean schools and you weren't getting any part of it? It was a hard pill to swallow because as a business that complies with every legislation we obviously did not get to that opportunity. D: What would be an average quote? I would say roughly R2-R4.50 per square meter. So my math is right, just over R10,000, P: Just over 10000, and there is no way you can do it for R200,00. It’s a scam. The SIU found that few contractors were registered with the Central Supplier Database or CSD - an approved list of government service providers. One of the things we found is out of 280 companies think about 173 were not on the CSD And for us it's a problem because then you find car washes, find companies that you don't understand how they go to this? We found that the money got in and they are spending it like hotcakes. And for us, it was a concern if we wait for the end of the investigation, this money wouldn't be there. Therefore, it's better we then go and block this amount of money before it gets out of the accounts In early June the SIU approached the Special Tribunal which was set up by the National Prosecuting Authority to fast-track high profile cases. Carte Blanche accessed the preservation orders issued to freeze bank accounts and assets to the value of R40.7 million of 14 service providers, this was followed a week later by 7 more companies with assets worth R22.4 million. The SIU investigators highlighted several characters in their affidavits, like Durban HIV researcher Dr Sigwile Bright Mhlongo, whose four companies [Insimu Projects, which was awarded a R13.9m contract; Insimu Consulting (R11.5m); Mangaliso Projects (R11.6m); and Insimu Medical Group (R4.6m)] received R41 million. His businesses are part of a Durban-based Foundation which owns several hospitals and businesses [Umlazi Private Hospital, Roodepoort Urogynae Hospital, a paramedic company, an agricultural foundation, medical equipment and linen manufacturing companies and Men's Sexual Health Clinics SA.] It’s co-directors are Fikile Eugenia Mpofana and Dr Njabulo Mabaso who share a property in this Dainfern estate. Two of Mpofana's companies scored contracts worth R15.5m [Fikile Mpofana 11.6m and Lisondalo 3.9m] and were registered shortly before the awarding of the tenders. Lindokuhle Mkhize whose company, Mhlongo was a former director of, landed a R6.7m contract. After which Mkhize transferred R2.3m to Mhlongo. In a matter of weeks, 30 year old Mpofana and Dr Mhlongo burnt through over R40. In late October, Mpofana paid off her house (R705,000) bought a designer watches (R399,000 on Baume & Mercier watches at RLG Africa jewellers), jewellery (R190,800 on jewellery at Arthur Kaplan), a Mercedez Benz (R1.7m payment to EB Motors Klerksdorp for a Mercedes-Benz V-Class van) and plastic surgery (R143,000 to Johannesburg plastic surgeon Dr Deon Weyers). One of Mhlongo’s company bank accounts had just R1,000 in it before the department paid R11.6m. His spending included millions in investment policies, R2.5m payment into a Liberty Group policy; R3.5m payment into an Investec Wealth and Investment account), and two vehicles (R1.4m to EB Motors Klerksdorp for a Mercedes-Benz V-Class van, R775,037 for a Range Rover Sport) We called Dr Mhlongo and Fikile Mpofana. Mhlongo: “I can’t comment now as its under investigation. S: But you understand why people are upset, because it’s public money? Please speak to my lawyer.” S: “Do you have anything you want to add? Mpofana: No nothing. Thank-you.” Lawyer Siphile Buthelezi represents all of those we’ve named. They declined to comment and will file their responses to these allegations in court in due course. Buthelezi“The SIU has not plead any wrongdoing from our clients, S: Did your clients have any relationship with the department? B: They didn’t know anyone there. There’s 280 companies that were awarded.” In writing he added: "....the allegations are denied.” THE BIG QUESTION IS WHO SHOULD BE HELD ACCOUNTABLE? SOMEONE MADE THE DECISIONS WITHIN THE GAUTENG DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION 1. AS TO WHICH SERVICE PROVIDERS WOULD BE AWARDED THESE CONTRACTS, AND 2. THAT THE CLEANING METHOD WOULD PREDOMINANTLY BE FOGGING. Digging into the SIUs affidavits a Gauteng education department employee claims Nkhensani Hudson Baloyi was the one issuing instructions. AS HEAD OF DEPARTMENT EDWARD MOSUWE SIGNED OFF ON THE PROCUREMENT PROCESSES AND REVIEWED THE PAYMENTS. WHAT HAS HE GOT TO SAY? Mosuwe: “I’m in a meeting… I’m waiting for investigation and report.” Mosuwe’s mandate is to report everything to MEC Lesufi. Whilst, there is a separation of powers between the political head, and the administrative head, the head of department, that there has to be oversight. Carte Blanche approached Corruption Watch researcher Kirsten Pearson to request any meeting minutes that can indicate when the decisions were made and by whom. D: Has it been a reversal in transparency in regards to procurement information? Yes, unfortunately, the expenditure disclosure reports for helping have not been put out since January. It's now June. They were incredibly quick to respond they will be published after being audited. We hope they've not been editing the reports after all this time. The Gauteng Education Department responded on behalf of Baloyi and management saying it prefers to wait for the SIUs report before commenting… ”We eagerly await the findings and recommendations of the report so that we can act on them.” The Public Finance Management Act gives us some clues as to who should be held accountable. The accounting officer is the head of department and those who were involved in writing up the terms of reference for the work. Heywood made an additional discovery in the Gauteng expenditure disclosure report figures. M: I was able to pick up in the last of the reports that I analyzed a miscalculation of two hundred and fifty million rand, they were faithfully reproduced by the national treasury as if they were accurate, what's to stop the person, a person or persons dipping in at a later point and saying, well, they inflated by two hundred and fifty million rand, it's been accepted. We can now go and cash in on some of this money. The SIU wants to develop new laws in order to pursue corrupt officials' assets. Their investigations will be handed to the NPA who can then prosecute. We don't investigate people. we're investigating the contract between the department and those service providers. And if in the process we find the people we're calling them and hear their side of the story from the lowest level to the highest level. if the evidence leads us to you, we will come to you. On Wednesday this week, a third batch of asset seizures involving 5 new companies worth R4.5million was successfully granted. Bringing the total to over R67 million that the SIU are attempting to recoup.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Half a billion rand was spent cleaning schools potentially infected with covid, the method used - fogging - is scientifically unproven, turns out this was just dirty corruption.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: 2,300-3000 Gauteng schools were supposedly cleaned when schools went back last year after lockdown level 4 opened. (Thousands of school children and teachers, cleaners etc and unions were concerned about covid – everyone was panicking and so the Gauteng dept of education decided to clean schools – a decision was made to fog them, once they were fogged a "certificate of cleaning" was given to the school by the service provider). Despite the National dept of health issuing an advisory (second page) against fogging – as it doesn’t work, and they don’t require a certificate of cleaning (The certificate of cleaning came about when service providers were issuing these meaningless certificates that you have no covid… “guarantee that there’s no covid in the place we just cleaned... which is an insane thing to promise) Health experts, papers, reports around the world say fogging doesn’t work – no scientific evidence, and that normal cleaning and disinfection is best. Its never been recommended either by our local cleaning industry. We will show these normal cleaning methods... Contract never went out, they used the emergency procurement issue to sidestep the process. And 6 companies awarded these cleaning tenders worth R431 million just for the schools, and later on some provincial buildings R117 million which took the figure to over half a billion. 95% profit margin in this work according to bath… 40 million – only 2 million doing work…they’ve done costing… THE COMPANIES: The SIU are dealing with three batches – Asset forfeiture for over R40 million – KZN doctors – who were awarded contracts in gauteng… get names listed… main indiv. Dr Bright Mhalangu – director of 30 companies – the entity awarded the majority of the work had R1000 in its bank account and it received 11 million from gde. They find out that it was aid for jewellery, cars, watches, investment policies, paying off bonds. Source: Typically this is for labour, equipment and consumables. Second batch – R20 million 3rd batch – whistle-blower one of them… consulted in general. Work in progress. Only 5% would be actual costs… worse than the PPE one, they had to buy the masks… The Gauteng Exp disclosure report (publicised in daily maverick) was the key document – came out in sometime in early jan. This showed who got the contracts. Mark Heywood… A lot of these companies were est relatively recently, and have no track record. They weren’t included with NCCA – PAYING BELOW minimum wage, didn’t make contributions to industry for em – weren’t in accordance to regulations in the land. They select someone from CID (national treasury database) paul roux screen shots of suppliers…– they weren’t even on there, and if they were on there it was just before. Clearly handpicked… (paul roux – with documents) Logical conclusion is that they were politically connected…
metadata.Summary: KEO Group – paid R39.9-million KEO Group’s website bills the company as “an electrical mechanical and civil engineering also in the business of cleaning and hygiene services as well as smart technology sensitizer dispenser supplies and installation. We also offer services in project management, technical advisory and tender document management.” The website details offering “microbial fogs”. Among the claims are that these “prevent the build-up of pathogens … All have been tested and documented by the South African Bureau of Standards.” [There is no list or reference for this claim.] In correspondence project manager Geoffrey Nyathi said the company charged R10.25 per metre and did work for GDID over 27 weeks. The company’s current sole director is registered as 25-year-old Phetogo Molefe. Her name, however, doesn’t appear on the employee list Nyathi provided. The business address is listed as 87 Booysens Road, Booysens, in Johannesburg, and also indicates its address as unit numbers in an “Xspace” storage facility on the same street. If you visist both sites; one appeared to be a tyre workshop and the other a storage unit warehouse. The KEO Group website gallery shows uncaptioned photographs of what it states are examples of its projects. There is only one captioned picture on the website, of a person in a hazmat suit appearing to fog an office. It states “Kempton Park Department of Social Development” and is dated 23 June 2020.
metadata.Further information: Industry sources say the KEO Group does not have a track record in the office cleaning industry, that it has a very small number of employees and does not contract out its work, raising questions about it’s ability to have carried out the work for which it received the tender. The sources also allege that KEO has several outstanding compliance issues, including paying legislated pay rates, statutory contributions to the SARS skills levy and provident fund contributions. Cocase South Africa – paid R33.7-million Cocase South Africa is registered to Carol Cebile Blake and the business address is a house on Ivan Street in Kempton Park. The company’s online profile is a Facebook page. Its most recent post was a recruitment advertisement on 27 May 2020 for two environmental project managers. The page includes a link to a company website but this link is broken. Ambroser Solutions – paid R28.8-million The sole director of the company is listed as 32-year-old Simtholile Ambitious Ndlovu. The company was registered in February 2015 to an address in Highveld Park, Emalahleni, Mpumalanga. Ambroser Solutions’s only web presence turns out to be a listing with the National Contract Cleaning Association. It appears under “cleaner” with a physical address stated as Waterfront Blue Gill, 12 Dabchick Close, Kempton Park. The address doesn’t show up on a location map. Lucage Trading and Projects – paid R10.5-million This company has two directors listed as Magdeline Kagiso Kwele, 33, and Nsizwa Louis Mahlangu, 37, of Hatfield, Pretoria, and Pretoria West respectively. Their business address for Lucage Trading and Projects is listed as Chromeville Street in Mhluzi, Mpumalanga and the business was registered in June 2016. The email for the pair is registered to a university student number email. There is no web presence for the company though Lucage Trading and Projects appears on a public business listing site. There is no physical or postal address or contact details given here either. TES Cleaning – paid R3.8-million TES Cleaning was registered in November 2019. Its sole director is named as 38-year-old Kathy Singh of Douglasdale, Johannesburg. There is no web presence for the company and no publicly available contact details. The over R190-million spent by the GDID does not include the R431-million spent by the Gauteng Education Department on sanitising schools, which is still being investigated by the Special Investigating Unit (SIU). There were many more… RENTOKILL – fogging and another company that does fogging - we will ask them to show us fogging... need visuals... CDC video clip states it unequivocally … it does not work Mark Heywood: Then we received 1 or 2 extra reports, and then we came across the fact that the figures were inaccurate, out by R250,000. (mark’s article) – this was directed back to Gauteng treasury. Needed to go back to their figures. Then the disclosure reports went silent. Via PAIA by Kirsten at CW they will release it end of June. Bidvest prestige clean and disinfect 1,000 schools free of charge. Kirsten from corruption watch: Never seen such a quick reaction to paia request… lit a fire under the asses… We suspect they’ve still paid suppliers for de-fogging. But there has likely been a curtailing effect…def for jan/feb… Had they not been as active – in 2nd and 3rd waves to defog buildings and schools… central Johannesburg provisional buildings… paul roux…
